narrative.overview: The Command Center is rendered as the working paper of a stage manager: one book that coordinates every department of a role. Every connected tool becomes a department (Email, Projects, Design), every workflow is a numbered cue (Q-01, Q-02), and every state is stamped, never charted. The surface is warm stock paper under ink hairlines, deliberately flat and printed, with the signal-red STANDBY/GO call lamp as the only saturated primary. The world is crafted for a busy professional who fights tab sprawl: it earns trust through the calm authority of a rehearsal document, not through dashboard chrome. Motion is one authored cue (standby to go), status is stamped, depth is a soft offset shadow for the object only. Translating every state to the book's vocabulary: tasks are cue lines, tools are departments, statuses are rubber-stamps, roles are tabbed dividers.
keyCharacteristics: Printed-paper world: warm stock, ink hairlines, feTurbulence grain, no glass or glow except the red call lamp
Statuses are stamps and caps, never sparklines, progress rings, or charts
Departments are reusable-looking dot colors: blue=email, green=projects, amber=design
All display text is Big Shoulders, all cues/stamps/mono are IBM Plex Mono
A single authored cue motion (STANDBY → GO), respecting prefers-reduced-motion

rules.name: The Call-Lamp Rule
rules.body: Red appears on the page only where a live call or primary action sits. Its rarity is the point — a page with scattered red has lost its single voice.

rules.name: The One-Surface Rule
rules.body: Shadows belong on exactly one hero object (the open book); everywhere else depth is line and stock, never a floating box.

rules.name: The One-Lift Rule
rules.body: One object carries shadow and depth; the rest are flat, printed paper. A second shadowed element says the world is 3D, and it isn't.

dos: Do label demo data (a rotated "Synthetic demo" stamp) and keep invented commercial claims absent.
Do use the red lamp once and once only.
Do track line count: type as the rule of the book (STANDBY / GO / HOLD), never a number chart.
Do lead sections with a heading that carries its own weight — no kicker above it.
donts: Don't hide the persuasive hero inside a generic card stack or wrap it in hero-metric stats.
Don't introduce a system display face or gradient text.
Don't orbit a hero with a side stripe / hard offset shadow; depth is one lift.
Don't ship glyph/emoji icon tiles; a department is a dot and a label, not an icon grid.
